9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.
327	
328	## Final report (your last message)
329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340	
341	## Cleaning up the work (you decide, via subagents)
342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):
347	
348	- **janitor** — workspace hygiene: roadmap/READMEs concise, inbox from overflowing.
349	- **ground** — workspace-wide strategy, graph, ledger, and convergence review.
350	- **work-reviewer** — fresh-context review of your last work; is it converging?
351	- **blueprint** — Lean ↔ blueprint statement/`\uses` correctness for a scoped slice.
352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.
353	
354	Keep proving; delegate the upkeep.
355

11	/-!
12	# Cover independence for section-cut evaluation divisors
13	
14	The evaluation divisor used by the arbitrary-scheme `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`
15	producer is cut from an actual glued section.  Pulling such a divisor through an affine
16	coefficient change retains the pulled-back pointed cover, whereas the direct construction
17	uses the canonical pointed cover of the base-changed cocycle datum.  This file supplies the
18	pure refinement step between those covers: local equations cut by the same section on any
19	two subordinated pointed covers are `DivEq`.
20	
21	The comparison unit is the datum's transition unit restricted to the common refinement.
22	Thus this result records construction-level divisor equality, not merely equality of Picard
23	classes, and assumes neither `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented` nor a pullback square.
24	-/
25	
26	set_option autoImplicit false
27	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
28	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
29	
30	universe u
31	
32	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
33	
34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
35	
36	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule
37	
38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
39	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
40	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k}
41	
42	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
43	
44	/-- Local equations cut by one glued section are independent, up to `DivEq`, of the
45	subordinated pointed cover used to write them.  The witness is the intersection cover and
46	the restricted transition unit between the two selected datum pieces. -/
47	theorem sectionLocalEquations_divEq_of_same_section
48	    [IsAffineHom pi]
49	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
50	    (s : ↑(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
51	    (W W' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover)
52	    (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
53	    (hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B, W.opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ x))
54	    (hσ' : ∀ x : relCurve C B, W'.opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ' x))
55	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (x : relCurve C B) (hx : x ∈ D.pieces j),
56	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) x hx).hom (D.component s j)
57	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk x)) :
58	    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
59	      (D.sectionLocalEquations s W σ hσ hreg)
60	      (D.sectionLocalEquations s W' σ' hσ' hreg) := by
61	  refine ⟨W ⊓ W', (fun _ => inf_le_left), (fun _ => inf_le_right), fun x => ?_⟩
62	  have hleft : (W ⊓ W').opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ x) :=
63	    inf_le_left.trans (hσ x)
64	  have hright : (W ⊓ W').opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ' x) :=
65	    inf_le_right.trans (hσ' x)
66	  have hoverlap : (W ⊓ W').opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ x) ⊓ D.pieces (σ' x) :=
67	    le_inf hleft hright
68	  have htriple : (W ⊓ W').opens x ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ x) ⊓ D.pieces (σ' x) :=
69	    le_inf (le_inf le_top hleft) hright
70	  refine ⟨(relCurve C B).unitsRestrict hoverlap (D.unit (σ x) (σ' x)), ?_⟩
71	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom htriple)
72	    (s.property (σ x) (σ' x))
73	  rw [map_mul] at key
74	  simp only [sectionLocalEquations_eqn]
75	  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
76	      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ x) (D.component s (σ x))) =
77	    ((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict hoverlap (D.unit (σ x) (σ' x)) :
78	      Γ(relCurve C B, (W ⊓ W').opens x)) *
79	      (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
80	        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ' x) (D.component s (σ' x)))
81	  rw [show (((relCurve C B).unitsRestrict hoverlap (D.unit (σ x) (σ' x)) :
82	      Γ(relCurve C B, (W ⊓ W').opens x)ˣ) : Γ(relCurve C B, (W ⊓ W').opens x)) =
83	        (relCurve C B).resHom hoverlap
84	          (D.unit (σ x) (σ' x) : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces (σ x) ⊓ D.pieces (σ' x)))
85	      from rfl, BasicOpenCocycleDatum.component, BasicOpenCocycleDatum.component]
86	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key ⊢
87	  exact key

89	/-! ## Coefficient-change naturality -/
90	
91	/-- Restricting the datum-piece comparison to the actual preimage piece gives the
92	arbitrary-affine section comparison.  This is the pointwise equation bridge between the
93	base-changed glued section and `LocalEquations.pullbackEqn`. -/
94	theorem resHom_piecesMap_eq_relAffSectionsMap
95	    [IsAffineHom pi]
96	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
97	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
98	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] (j : D.index)
99	    (t : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j)) :
100	    (relCurve C B').resHom
101	        (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces_baseChange B' j).ge
102	        (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap B' j t) =
103	      relAffSectionsMap C B' (D.pieces j) t := by
104	  cases j with
105	  | inl j =>
106	      simpa only [BasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap, pieceSectionsMap,
107	        BasicOpenCoverData.pieces, BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange, Sum.elim_inl,
108	        relAffSectionsMap, Scheme.resHom_refl] using
109	        ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE_resHom
110	          (le_rfl : D.pieces (Sum.inl j) ≤ D.pieces (Sum.inl j))
111	          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage B' (Sum.inl j))
112	          (le_rfl : relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces (Sum.inl j) ≤
113	            relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces (Sum.inl j))
114	          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces_baseChange B' (Sum.inl j)).ge t)
115	  | inr j =>
116	      simpa only [BasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap, pieceSectionsMap,
117	        BasicOpenCoverData.pieces, BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange, Sum.elim_inr,
118	        relAffSectionsMap, Scheme.resHom_refl] using
119	        ((relCurveMap C B B').appLE_resHom
120	          (le_rfl : D.pieces (Sum.inr j) ≤ D.pieces (Sum.inr j))
121	          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage B' (Sum.inr j))
122	          (le_rfl : relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces (Sum.inr j) ≤
123	            relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces (Sum.inr j))
124	          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieces_baseChange B' (Sum.inr j)).ge t)
125	
126	/-- The equation obtained by pulling back the canonical section-cut local equations is the
127	arbitrary-affine comparison of the selected datum component. -/
128	theorem pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquations_eq_relAffSectionsMap
129	    [IsFinite pi] [IsNoetherianRing B]
130	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
131	    (s : ↑(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
132	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
133	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
134	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
135	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] (z : relCurve C B') :
136	    Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C B B')
137	        (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib) z =
138	      relAffSectionsMap C B'
139	        (D.pieces (D.pieceIndex ((relCurveMap C B B').base z)))
140	        (D.component s (D.pieceIndex ((relCurveMap C B B').base z))) := by
141	  simp [Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn,
142	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular,
143	    BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations,
144	    relAffSectionsMap, Scheme.resHom]
145	
146	/-- Pulling back the divisor cut by a fibrewise-regular glued section is `DivEq` to the
147	divisor cut by the compared section on the canonical cover after an arbitrary affine
148	coefficient change.  The first comparison has unit `1` on the pulled cover; the second is
149	the transition-unit refinement supplied by `sectionLocalEquations_divEq_of_same_section`. -/
150	theorem pullback_sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_divEq_sectionsMapTop
151	    [IsFinite pi] [IsNoetherianRing B]
152	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
153	    (s : ↑(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
154	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
155	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
156	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
157	    [IsScalarTower k B B'] [IsNoetherianRing B']
158	    (hfib' : ∀ (j : (D.baseChange B').index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B'),
159	      Function.Injective
160	        ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B'
161	          ((D.baseChange B').component (D.sectionsMapTop B' s) j)).rTensor
162	            p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
163	    (hpull : ∀ (y z : relCurve C B')
164	      (hz : z ∈ ((D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).cover.pullback
165	        (relCurveMap C B B')).opens y),
166	      ((relCurve C B').presheaf.germ
167	        (((D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).cover.pullback
168	          (relCurveMap C B B')).opens y) z hz).hom
169	          (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C B B')
170	            (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib) y) ∈
171	        nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B').presheaf.stalk z)) :
172	    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq
173	      ((D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).pullback
174	        (relCurveMap C B B') hpull)
175	      ((D.baseChange B').sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
176	        (D.sectionsMapTop B' s) hfib') := by
177	  let f := relCurveMap C B B'
178	  let W := D.pointedCover.pullback f
179	  let sigma : relCurve C B' → D.index := fun z => D.pieceIndex (f.base z)
180	  let hsigma : ∀ z : relCurve C B', W.opens z ≤ (D.baseChange B').pieces (sigma z) :=
181	    fun z => D.pullback_pointedCover_le B' z
182	  let s' := D.sectionsMapTop B' s
183	  let hreg' : ∀ (j : (D.baseChange B').index) (z : relCurve C B')
184	      (hz : z ∈ (D.baseChange B').pieces j),
185	      ((relCurve C B').presheaf.germ ((D.baseChange B').pieces j) z hz).hom
186	          ((D.baseChange B').component s' j) ∈
187	        nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B').presheaf.stalk z) :=
188	    fun j z hz =>
189	      (D.baseChange B').germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s' j (hfib' j) z hz
190	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq.trans (d₂ :=
191	    (D.baseChange B').sectionLocalEquations s' W sigma hsigma hreg') ?_ ?_
192	  · refine ⟨W, (fun _ => le_rfl), (fun _ => le_rfl), fun z => ?_⟩
193	    refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
194	    rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]
195	    simp only [Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback_eqn, sectionLocalEquations_eqn]
196	    rw [D.pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquations_eq_relAffSectionsMap s hfib B' z]
197	    rw [D.component_sectionsMapTop B' s (sigma z)]
198	    apply congrArg ((relCurve C B').resHom _)
199	    exact (D.resHom_piecesMap_eq_relAffSectionsMap B' (sigma z)
200	      (D.component s (sigma z))).symm
201	  · simpa only [BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular,
202	      s', hreg'] using
203	      (D.baseChange B').sectionLocalEquations_divEq_of_same_section s'
204	        W (D.baseChange B').pointedCover sigma (D.baseChange B').pieceIndex
205	        hsigma (fun _ => le_rfl) hreg'
206	
207	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

9	/-!
10	# Sections to divisors — the LocalEquations construction and the class law (DAT-A)
11	
12	Worksheet §2.2 step 2, made literal (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §3): a global section of
13	the DAT-1 glued sheaf **is** a matching family `(s_j)` with `s_i = g_{ij}·s_j`, so once
14	its components are germ-regular (DAT-A2, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisors`)
15	it is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on the nose. The (1e) class law
16	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafClass.lean`, landed while this brick was in flight) is consumed
17	directly — the spec's `cocycleClassOn` seam is CLOSED, no interim class carrier exists:
18	
19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations` — the LocalEquations datum of a
20	  germ-regular global section on **any** pointed cover subordinated to the pieces
21	  (the (1e) subordination interface `𝒲, σ, hσ`): equations the restricted components
22	  `D.component s (σ y)`, ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units
23	  `gluedSubordUnit`;
24	* `sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit` — the ratio units are **exactly** the (restricted)
25	  transition units of the cocycle (`ratioUnit_unique`); on the piece cover the
26	  restriction is along `≤`-reflexivity, i.e. the units themselves;
27	* `sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle` — the units cocycle of the constructed datum is
28	  the (1e) subordinated cocycle `gluedSubordCocycle`;
29	* **the class law** `sectionLocalEquations_picClass`:
30	  `(D.sectionLocalEquations …).picClass = D.cechPicClass` — the divisor datum cut out
31	  by a germ-regular section presents THE class of the datum's cocycle (the Abel
32	  correspondence), through the landed `cechPicClass_eq_mk`. Naturality under
33	  refinement/subordination-choice is the landed `gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq`; unit
34	  rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the
35	  landed `LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`;
36	* `sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr` — any two germ-regular sections on any two
37	  subordinated covers cut divisors of the same class;
38	* `sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular` — the A2-bundled wrapper on the canonical
39	  pointed cover (`D.pointedCover`): a fibrewise-regular global section yields the
40	  divisor datum outright, with class `D.cechPicClass` (`[IsNoetherianRing B]`).
41	-/

55	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

57	
58	/-- The value of a restricted unit section is the restriction of its value. -/
59	private lemma val_unitsRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} {W U : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U)
60	    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
61	    ((X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) = X.resHom h (u : Γ(X, U)) :=
62	  rfl

64	section AffineHom

66	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
67	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
68	variable (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
69	variable (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
70	variable (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
71	
72	/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps
73	of a subordinated pointed cover: the matching relation of the glued family, restricted
74	from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
75	private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
76	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom
78	        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
79	      = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
80	            Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
81	        * ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
82	            𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y')).op).hom
83	            ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y'))) := by
84	  have hle : 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'
85	      ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ y) ⊓ D.pieces (σ y') :=
86	    le_inf (le_inf le_top (inf_le_left.trans (hσ y))) (inf_le_right.trans (hσ y'))
87	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom hle) (s.property (σ y) (σ y'))
88	  rw [map_mul] at key
89	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
90	  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
91	      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
92	    = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
93	        Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
94	      * (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
95	          ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y')))
96	  rw [gluedSubordUnit, val_unitsRestrict, component, component]
97	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
98	  exact key
99	
100	/-- **Sections ↦ divisor families** (DAT-A, worksheet §2.2 step 2): a germ-regular
101	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on any
102	pointed cover subordinated to the pieces — the equations are the (restricted)
103	components, the ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units. Germ-regularity
104	(`hreg`) is DAT-A2's output (`germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors` relatively;
105	`Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero` on an integral field-level curve). -/
106	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquations
107	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
108	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
109	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
110	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations where
111	  cover := 𝒲
112	  eqn y := (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y))
113	  regular y z hz := by
114	    rw [Scheme.resHom, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
115	    exact hreg (σ y) z (hσ y hz)
116	  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
117	    ⟨gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y', D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y'⟩
118	
119	variable (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
120	  ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
121	    ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
122	
123	@[simp]
124	lemma sectionLocalEquations_cover :
125	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).cover = 𝒲 :=
126	  rfl
127	
128	@[simp]
129	lemma sectionLocalEquations_eqn (y : relCurve C B) :
130	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).eqn y
131	      = (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)) :=
132	  rfl
133	
134	/-- **The ratio units are exactly the cocycle's transition units** (worksheet §2.2 step
135	2's "ratio units EXACTLY the cocycle"), in subordinated form: by uniqueness of ratio
136	witnesses against a regular equation. On the piece cover the subordination is
137	`≤`-reflexivity and `gluedSubordUnit` is the transition unit restricted along it. -/
138	lemma sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit (y y' : relCurve C B) :
139	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit y y'
140	      = gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :=
141	  ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y'
142	    (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y')
143	    (D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y')).symm
144	
145	/-- The units cocycle of the constructed LocalEquations datum is the (1e) subordinated
146	cocycle of the datum. -/
147	lemma sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle :
148	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle
149	      = gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ :=
150	  Scheme.unitsCocycle_ext fun y y' =>
151	    ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle_evInf y y').trans
152	      ((D.sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg y y').trans
153	        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ y y').symm)
154	
155	/-- **THE CLASS LAW** (DAT-A keystone; the Abel correspondence of worksheet §2.2 step
156	2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of
157	the DAT-1 glued sheaf is THE Čech Picard class of the datum's cocycle (stage (1e),
158	consumed on the nose through `cechPicClass_eq_mk`). -/
159	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass :
160	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass = D.cechPicClass := by
161	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
162	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
163	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]
164	  exact D.cechPicClass_eq_mk 𝒲 σ hσ
165	
166	end AffineHom
167	
168	/-- **Independence of the section and the cover** (refinement/rescaling naturality,
169	subsumed): the class of the divisor datum cut by ANY germ-regular section of the datum,
170	on ANY subordinated pointed cover, is the same — both are `D.cechPicClass`. Unit
171	rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the landed
172	`LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`. -/
173	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
174	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
175	    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
176	    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
177	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
178	    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
179	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
180	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
181	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))
182	    (hreg' : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
183	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
184	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
185	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
186	      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
187	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
188	    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']
189	
190	/-! ## The A2-bundled wrapper, on the canonical pointed cover -/
191	
192	section Bundled
193	
194	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
195	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
196	
197	/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
198	Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
199	yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its
200	class is `D.cechPicClass` (`sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass`). -/
201	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
202	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
203	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
204	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
205	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
206	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
207	  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
208	    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)
209	
210	/-- The class law for the A2-bundled wrapper: the fibrewise-regular section cuts a
211	divisor of class exactly the datum's (1e) class. -/
212	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass
213	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
214	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
215	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
216	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
217	    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=
218	  D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) _
219	
220	end Bundled
221	
222	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
223	
224	end AlgebraicGeometry

21	namespace BasicOpenCoverData
22	
23	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
24	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
25	variable (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
26	  [IsScalarTower k B B']
27	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
28	variable (D : BasicOpenCoverData C B pi)
29	
30	/-- The comparison of sections on a datum piece with sections on its base change. -/
31	noncomputable def piecesMap : ∀ j : D.index,
32	    Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) →+*
33	      Γ(relCurve C B', (D.baseChange B').pieces j)
34	  | .inl j => pieceSectionsMap B' (fiberChart₀ pi) (D.h₀ j)
35	  | .inr j => pieceSectionsMap B' (fiberChart₁ pi) (D.h₁ j)
36	
37	/-- Base change commutes with the basic-open localization defining each datum piece. -/
38	noncomputable def pieceTermBaseChange : ∀ j : D.index,
39	    B' ⊗[B] Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ≃ₐ[B']
40	      Γ(relCurve C B', (D.baseChange B').pieces j)
41	  | .inl j =>
42	      pieceTermBaseChangeAlg B' (fiberChart₀ pi)
43	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isCompact
44	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isQuasiSeparated
45	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
46	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₀ j)
47	  | .inr j =>
48	      pieceTermBaseChangeAlg B' (fiberChart₁ pi)
49	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isCompact
50	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isQuasiSeparated
51	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
52	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₁ j)
53	
54	/-- The datum-piece base-change equivalence sends `1 ⊗ t` to the compared section. -/
55	theorem pieceTermBaseChange_one_tmul (j : D.index)
56	    (t : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j)) :
57	    D.pieceTermBaseChange B' j ((1 : B') ⊗ₜ[B] t) = D.piecesMap B' j t := by
58	  cases j with
59	  | inl j =>
60	      exact pieceTermBaseChangeAlg_one_tmul B' (fiberChart₀ pi)
61	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isCompact
62	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₀.isQuasiSeparated
63	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
64	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₀ j) t
65	  | inr j =>
66	      exact pieceTermBaseChangeAlg_one_tmul B' (fiberChart₁ pi)
67	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isCompact
68	        (fiberTwoCover pi).isAffineOpen₁.isQuasiSeparated
69	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B (fiberTwoCover pi))
70	        (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C B' (fiberTwoCover pi)) (D.h₁ j) t
71	
72	end BasicOpenCoverData
73	
74	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
75	
76	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
77	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
78	variable (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
79	  [IsScalarTower k B B']
80	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom pi]
81	
82	/-- Compare a global glued section along a change of coefficient ring. -/
83	noncomputable def sectionsMapTop (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
84	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) :
85	    ↥(gluedSubmodule B' (D.baseChange B').pieces (D.baseChange B').unit ⊤) :=
86	  D.sectionsMap B' (by rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]) s
87	
88	/-- Components of the compared global section are the compared original components. -/
89	theorem component_sectionsMapTop (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
90	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (j : D.index) :
91	    (D.baseChange B').component (D.sectionsMapTop B' s) j =
92	      D.toBasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap B' j (D.component s j) := by
93	  let htop : (⊤ : (relCurve C B').Opens) ≤
94	      relCurveMap C B B' ⁻¹ᵁ (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens) := by
95	    rw [Scheme.Hom.preimage_top]
96	  cases j with
97	  | inl j =>
98	      simpa only [sectionsMapTop, component, sectionsMap_coe,
99	        BasicOpenCocycleDatum.baseChange, BasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap,
100	        BasicOpenCoverData.pieces, BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange,
101	        Sum.elim_inl, pieceSectionsMap] using
102	        (relCurveMap C B B').appLE_resHom
103	          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : D.pieces (Sum.inl j) ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (Sum.inl j))
104	          (D.sectionsMap_component_le B' htop (Sum.inl j))
105	          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage B' (Sum.inl j))
106	          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inl j) ≤
107	            ⊤ ⊓ (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inl j)) (s.val (Sum.inl j))
108	  | inr j =>
109	      simpa only [sectionsMapTop, component, sectionsMap_coe,
110	        BasicOpenCocycleDatum.baseChange, BasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap,
111	        BasicOpenCoverData.pieces, BasicOpenCoverData.baseChange,
112	        Sum.elim_inr, pieceSectionsMap] using
113	        (relCurveMap C B B').appLE_resHom
114	          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : D.pieces (Sum.inr j) ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (Sum.inr j))
115	          (D.sectionsMap_component_le B' htop (Sum.inr j))
116	          (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.baseChange_pieces_le_preimage B' (Sum.inr j))
117	          (le_inf le_top le_rfl : (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inr j) ≤
118	            ⊤ ⊓ (D.baseChange B').pieces (Sum.inr j)) (s.val (Sum.inr j))
119	
120	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
121	
122	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
123	-- The glued trivialization carries a large dependent family of section rings.
124	-- A nonzero global section of a cocycle-glued line bundle on an integral scheme is
125	-- nonzero in every nonempty trivializing piece.
126	theorem component_ne_zero_of_global_ne_zero
127	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C K pi)
128	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule K D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (hs : s ≠ 0)
129	    (j : D.index) (hj : D.pieces j ≠ ⊥) : D.component s j ≠ 0 := by
130	  intro hcomponent
131	  apply hs
132	  have hUj : ((D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
133	    rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C K)) with h | h
134	    · exact (hj (by ext x; rw [h]; simp)).elim
135	    · exact h
136	  have hres : gluedRes K D.pieces D.unit (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ ⊤) s = 0 := by
137	    apply (gluedTriv K D.isGluingCocycle j le_rfl).injective
138	    rw [map_zero, gluedTriv_apply, gluedRes_coe]
139	    simpa only [component, Scheme.resHom_resHom] using hcomponent
140	  apply Subtype.ext
141	  funext i
142	  by_cases hi : D.pieces i = ⊥
143	  · have hopen : ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i = ⊥ := by rw [hi]; simp
144	    letI : Subsingleton Γ(relCurve C K, ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i) := hopen ▸ inferInstance
145	    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _
146	  · have hUi : ((D.pieces i : Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
147	      rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty (D.pieces i : Set (relCurve C K)) with h | h
148	      · exact (hi (by ext x; rw [h]; simp)).elim
149	      · exact h
150	    have hUji : (((D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i : (relCurve C K).Opens) :
151	        Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
152	      simpa only [Opens.coe_inf] using
153	        nonempty_preirreducible_inter (D.pieces j).isOpen (D.pieces i).isOpen hUj hUi
154	    letI : Nonempty ↥((D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i : (relCurve C K).Opens) :
155	        Set (relCurve C K)) := by
156	      obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hUji
157	      exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩⟩
158	    have hinj : Function.Injective ((relCurve C K).resHom
159	        (show D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i by simp)) :=
160	      map_injective_of_isIntegral (H := this) (relCurve C K)
161	        (homOfLE (show D.pieces j ⊓ D.pieces i ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces i by simp))
162	    apply hinj
163	    have hval := congrArg (fun t => t.val i) hres
164	    simpa only [gluedRes_coe, Pi.zero_apply, Submodule.coe_zero, map_zero] using hval
165	
166	/-- Every component of a nonzero global cocycle-glued section on an integral scheme is
167	a nonzerodivisor, including the vacuous empty-piece case. -/
168	theorem component_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_global_ne_zero
169	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C K)] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C K pi)
170	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule K D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (hs : s ≠ 0) (j : D.index) :
171	    D.component s j ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C K, D.pieces j) := by
172	  by_cases hj : D.pieces j = ⊥
173	  · letI : Subsingleton Γ(relCurve C K, D.pieces j) := hj ▸ inferInstance
174	    rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
175	    intro z _
176	    exact Subsingleton.elim z 0
177	  · have hUj : ((D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C K))).Nonempty := by
178	      rcases Set.eq_empty_or_nonempty (D.pieces j : Set (relCurve C K)) with h | h
179	      · exact (hj (by ext x; rw [h]; simp)).elim
180	      · exact h
181	    let hnonempty : Nonempty {x : relCurve C K // x ∈ D.pieces j} := by
182	      obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hUj
183	      exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩⟩
184	    haveI : IsDomain Γ(relCurve C K, D.pieces j) :=
185	      @IsIntegral.component_integral (relCurve C K) _ (D.pieces j) hnonempty
186	    exact mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero
187	      (D.component_ne_zero_of_global_ne_zero s hs j hj)
188	
189	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
190	
191	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
192	-- Elaborating the tensor swap and piecewise base-change equivalence needs extra heartbeats.
193	theorem injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero
194	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
195	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤)) (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
196	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField)]
197	    (hs : D.sectionsMapTop p.asIdeal.ResidueField s ≠ 0) (j : D.index) :
198	    Function.Injective
199	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
200	  let e : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField ≃+*
201	      Γ(relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
202	        (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).pieces j) :=
203	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j)
204	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField).toRingEquiv.trans
205	        (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieceTermBaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField j).toRingEquiv
206	  have hvalue : e (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) =
207	      (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).component
208	        (D.sectionsMapTop p.asIdeal.ResidueField s) j := by
209	    change D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieceTermBaseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField j
210	      (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm B Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j)
211	        p.asIdeal.ResidueField
212	          (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField))) = _
213	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.comm_tmul,
214	      D.toBasicOpenCoverData.pieceTermBaseChange_one_tmul
215	        p.asIdeal.ResidueField j (D.component s j),
216	      ← D.component_sectionsMapTop p.asIdeal.ResidueField s j]
217	  have hregular : (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).component
218	        (D.sectionsMapTop p.asIdeal.ResidueField s) j ∈
219	      nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
220	        (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).pieces j) :=
221	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).component_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_global_ne_zero
222	      (D.sectionsMapTop p.asIdeal.ResidueField s) hs j
223	  have himage : e (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
224	      nonZeroDivisors Γ(relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
225	        (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).pieces j) := by
226	    rwa [hvalue]
227	  have hback : e.symm (e (D.component s j ⊗ₜ[B]
228	      (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField))) ∈
229	      nonZeroDivisors (Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
230	    rw [← MulEquivClass.map_nonZeroDivisors e.symm]
231	    exact ⟨_, himage, rfl⟩
232	  apply injective_rTensor_mulSectionEnd_of_tmul_mem_nonZeroDivisors B
233	    (D.component s j) p
234	  simpa only [e.symm_apply_apply] using hback
235	
236	end BasicOpenCocycleDatum
237	
238	end AlgebraicGeometry

11	/-!
12	# The widened divisor-functor map (R2, human decision I-0492)
13	
14	`DivFamZarAff.mapAlg` along an arbitrary test change `R → R'`, with the functor laws, the Abel
15	hook, and the Zariski separation keystone.  This is what makes the widened value a functor
16	VALUE rather than a bare type: before this file nothing could base-change a widened class.
17	
18	## Where the widening does and does not show
19	
20	Almost nowhere.  `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` widens where the pieces live on the CURVE and changes
21	nothing about the Zariski cover of the BASE, so the base-side machinery of
22	`DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg.lean` — the `Localization.Away` towers, `IsLocalization.map`,
23	`span_range_algebraMap_eq_top` — applies verbatim; the cover datum only appears inside the
24	opaque `mapAlg` of the local certified family.  Likewise
25	`Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback`, `divEq_pullback_id` and `divEq_pullback_pullback` are
26	stated for ARBITRARY scheme morphisms and know nothing about covers, so the functor laws are
27	the same three lines as in the chart-typed case.
28	
29	## The one honest cost of the widening: overlap affineness
30	
31	`AffCoverData` demands affineness of the pieces only (that is the R2 shape), so the certificate
32	transport takes an explicit `hinf` — the overlaps are affine.  A `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff`
33	therefore cannot be base-changed without it, and rather than weaken the structure this file
34	carries `hinf` as a hypothesis on `mapAlg` at the family level.  It is not a hidden
35	assumption: it is visible in every signature below, as I-0492 clause 4 requires.  For a
36	relative curve over a proper `C` it is discharged by separatedness (`IsAffineOpen.inf`).
37	
38	## Main declarations
39	
40	* `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.mapAlg` — base change of a widened certified family.
41	* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.pullback` — certificate transport along an arbitrary test change.
42	* `DivFamZarAff.mapAlg`, with `mapAlg_mk`, `picClass_mapAlg`, `mapAlg_id`, `mapAlg_comp`.
43	* `DivFamZarAff.eq_of_away_eq` — Zariski separation at the widened Zar level.
44	-/

62	/-- **Overlap affineness of a widened cover** — the one datum the certificate transport needs
63	beyond `AffCoverData`'s own fields.  Named so that it can be threaded explicitly and read off
64	any signature; for a relative curve over a proper `C` it follows from separatedness. -/
65	def AffCoverData.HasAffineOverlaps (D : AffCoverData C R) : Prop :=
66	  ∀ i j : D.index, IsAffineOpen (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j)

71	/-- **Base change of a widened certified family**: pulled equations, base-changed cover and
72	adaptation, transported certificate. -/
73	noncomputable def CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.mapAlg (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R n)
74	    (hinf : F.cover.HasAffineOverlaps) : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R' n where
75	  eqns := F.adaptation.pulledEquations R' F.certified.projective_colength
76	  cover := F.cover.baseChange R'
77	  adaptation := F.adaptation.pullback R' F.certified.projective_colength
78	  certified := F.adaptation.isCertified_pullback R' hinf F.certified
79	
80	@[simp]
81	lemma CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.mapAlg_cover (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R n)
82	    (hinf : F.cover.HasAffineOverlaps) :
83	    (F.mapAlg R' n hinf).cover = F.cover.baseChange R' := rfl
84	
85	/-- **The base-changed cover again has affine overlaps**: overlaps of base-changed pieces are
86	preimages of overlaps, and preimages of affine opens under `relCurveMap` are affine.  So the
87	`hinf` obligation propagates along a tower rather than accumulating. -/
88	theorem AffCoverData.hasAffineOverlaps_baseChange {D : AffCoverData C R}
89	    (hinf : D.HasAffineOverlaps) : (D.baseChange R').HasAffineOverlaps := fun i j => by
90	  rw [show (D.baseChange R').pieces i ⊓ (D.baseChange R').pieces j
91	      = relCurveMap C R R' ⁻¹ᵁ (D.pieces i ⊓ D.pieces j) from rfl]
92	  exact isAffineOpen_relCurveMap_preimage C R' (hinf i j)
93	
94	/-- **`HasAffineOverlaps` is FREE for a proper `C`** — which is the only case the DD-R lane
95	ever uses.  The relative curve over a proper `C` is a separated scheme, so its affine opens are
96	closed under intersection (`Over.isAffineOpen_inf`, via the affine diagonal).
97	
98	So the `hinf` threading below is bookkeeping, not a standing assumption: it is dischargeable
99	wherever `C` is proper, and it is stated rather than assumed so that a reader can see the cost
100	of `AffCoverData` demanding affineness of the pieces only. -/
101	theorem AffCoverData.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper [IsProper C.hom] (D : AffCoverData C R) :
102	    D.HasAffineOverlaps := fun i j =>
103	  Over.isAffineOpen_inf (A := R) C (D.isAffineOpen i) (D.isAffineOpen j)

107	/-- **Witness transport along a tower `R → A → B`**, widened: a certified family over `A`
108	divisor-equal to the pulled system stays divisor-equal after `mapAlg` to `B`.  Verbatim the
109	chart-typed `CertifiedDivisorFamily.divEq_mapAlg_pullback` — `divEq_pullback` along
110	`relCurveMap C A B`, then the composite collapse `divEq_pullback_pullback` at
111	`relCurveMap_comp`; both are statements about arbitrary scheme morphisms. -/
112	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.divEq_mapAlg_pullback
113	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra R A] [IsScalarTower k R A]
114	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra A B]
115	    [IsScalarTower k R B] [IsScalarTower k A B] [IsScalarTower R A B]
116	    (E : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C A n) (hinf : E.cover.HasAffineOverlaps)
117	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} {hregA} (hregB)
118	    (hdiv : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq E.eqns (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R A) hregA)) :
119	    Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq (E.mapAlg B n hinf).eqns
120	      (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R B) hregB) := by
121	  have hcomp : relCurveMap C A B ≫ relCurveMap C R A = relCurveMap C R B :=
122	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := A) (R'' := B)
123	  have hregMid := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_divEq
124	    (relCurveMap C A B) hdiv
125	    (E.adaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors B E.certified.projective_colength)
126	  exact Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq.trans
127	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C A B) hdiv
128	      (E.adaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors B
129	        E.certified.projective_colength) hregMid)
130	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback_pullback hcomp d hregA hregMid hregB)

133	
134	The widened analogue of `IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: a widened
135	locally certified system has regular pulled equations along an arbitrary test tower.
136	Regularity is germ-local on the curve, and the covering argument is on the BASE, so the proof
137	is the chart-typed one with `CertifiedDivisorFamily` replaced by
138	`CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff`. -/
139	
140	theorem IsLocallyCertifiedAff.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
141	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
142	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertifiedAff (C := C) (R := R) n d)
143	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
144	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
145	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
146	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
147	  classical
148	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
149	  haveI himm : ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin m),
150	      IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R'
151	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) := fun i =>
152	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R'
153	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
154	  have hspan' : Ideal.span (Set.range
155	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) = ⊤ := by
156	    have hrange : Set.range (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
157	        = algebraMap R R' '' Set.range g := by
158	      ext x
159	      exact ⟨by rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩; exact ⟨g i.down, ⟨i.down, rfl⟩, rfl⟩,
160	        by rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩; exact ⟨⟨j⟩, rfl⟩⟩
161	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
162	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_immersion_cover
163	    (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => relCurveMap C R'
164	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))
165	    (fun y' => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R'
166	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
167	      (fun i => Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) hspan' y')
168	    (relCurveMap C R R') d (fun i ζ => ?_) y z hz
169	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i.down
170	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) :=
171	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i.down)) (g i.down)
172	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i.down))
173	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
174	    (IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers (g i.down))
175	      (T := Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
176	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R')
177	      (by
178	        rintro x ⟨e, rfl⟩
179	        use e
180	        simp)).toAlgebra
181	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
182	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
183	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
184	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, IsLocalization.map_comp,
185	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq])
186	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (g i.down))
187	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
188	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
189	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R (Localization.Away (g i.down)),
190	        ← RingHom.comp_assoc,
191	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
192	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))),
193	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R
194	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))])
195	  have hcomp₁ : relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
196	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
197	      ≫ relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
198	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
199	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away (g i.down))
200	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
201	  have hcomp₂ : relCurveMap C R' (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
202	      ≫ relCurveMap C R R'
203	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
204	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := R')
205	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
206	  have step1 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_congr hcomp₂ d ζ
207	  have step2 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_comp hcomp₁ d
208	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
209	      (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) d) ζ
210	  have hfinal := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_self_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_divEq
211	    (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
212	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) hGdiv ζ
213	    (G.adaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
214	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
215	      G.certified.projective_colength ζ ζ
216	      ((G.eqns.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
217	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))).mem_opens ζ))
218	  exact ((step1.trans step2).symm ▸ hfinal)

221	
222	`IsProper C.hom` from here on: it is what makes `HasAffineOverlaps` free
223	(`hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper`), so no `hinf` appears in any statement below.  The DD-R lane

230	/-- **Certificate transport, widened** (the S5b keystone at `DivFamZarAff`): the widened
231	locally-certified predicate is stable under an ARBITRARY test change `R → R'`.
232	
233	The base-side argument is untouched by the widening — the pushed cover `algebraMap R R' ∘ g`
234	spans `⊤` and the certified part over each `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` is
235	`mapAlg` of the local family — because R2 widens where the pieces live on the CURVE and changes
236	nothing about the Zariski cover of the BASE.  Compare
237	`IsLocallyCertified.pullback` (`DivisorFamilyZarMapAlg.lean`): the proof is the same, with the
238	cover datum appearing only inside the opaque `mapAlg`. -/
239	theorem IsLocallyCertifiedAff.pullback {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
240	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) (hreg) :
241	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff (C := C) (R := R') n
242	      (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R R') hreg) := by
243	  classical
244	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
245	  have hloc' : IsLocallyCertifiedAff (C := C) (R := R) n d := ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩
246	  refine ⟨m, fun i => algebraMap R R' (g i), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
247	  · have hrange : (Set.range fun i : Fin m => algebraMap R R' (g i))
248	        = algebraMap R R' '' Set.range g := by
249	      ext x
250	      exact ⟨by rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩; exact ⟨g i, ⟨i, rfl⟩, rfl⟩,
251	        by rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩; exact ⟨j, rfl⟩⟩
252	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
253	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
254	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
255	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
256	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R'
257	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i)))) :=
258	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R'
259	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) (algebraMap R R' (g i))
260	  -- the induced away map as a local algebra tower
261	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i))
262	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) :=
263	    (IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers (g i))
264	      (T := Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R R' (g i)))
265	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) (algebraMap R R')
266	      (by
267	        rintro x ⟨e, rfl⟩
268	        use e
269	        simp)).toAlgebra
270	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away (g i))
271	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) :=
272	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
273	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, IsLocalization.map_comp,
274	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq])
275	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (g i))
276	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) :=
277	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
278	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R (Localization.Away (g i)),
279	        ← RingHom.comp_assoc,
280	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R (Localization.Away (g i))
281	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))),
282	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R
283	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i)))])
284	  -- witness transport along `R → Localization.Away (g i) → the pushed chart`
285	  have hW := G.divEq_mapAlg_pullback n (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i)))
286	    (G.cover.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper)
287	    (hloc'.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
288	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i)))) hGdiv
289	  -- the composite collapse through the `R'`-side factorization
290	  have hcomp₂ : relCurveMap C R' (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i)))
291	      ≫ relCurveMap C R R'
292	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) :=
293	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := R') (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i)))
294	  have hstep := Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback_pullback hcomp₂ d hreg
295	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
296	      (relCurveMap C R' (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))))
297	      (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R R') hreg))
298	    (hloc'.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
299	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))))
300	  exact ⟨G.mapAlg (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))) n
301	    (G.cover.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper), hW.trans hstep.symm⟩
302	
303	/-! ## The widened divisor-functor map -/
304	
305	/-- **The widened divisor-functor map on locally certified classes** along an ARBITRARY test
306	change: pull back the representative (the widened mapAlg-hreg engine discharges regularity) and
307	transport the certificates.  Well defined by `divEq_pullback`.
308	
309	With this, `DivFamZarAff` is a functor value: the field-uniform carrier of R2 base-changes
310	exactly as the chart-typed one did. -/
311	noncomputable def DivFamZarAff.mapAlg :
312	    DivFamZarAff C R n → DivFamZarAff C R' n :=
313	  Quotient.lift
314	    (fun dp : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d} =>
315	      DivFamZarAff.mk (dp.1.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')
316	          (dp.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors R' n))
317	        (dp.2.pullback R' n _))
318	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr
319	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R R') h _ _))
320	
321	@[simp]
322	lemma DivFamZarAff.mapAlg_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
323	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
324	    DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R' n (DivFamZarAff.mk d hd)
325	      = DivFamZarAff.mk (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')
326	          (hd.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors R' n))
327	        (hd.pullback R' n _) :=
328	  rfl

330	/-- **The Abel-hook class law at the widened Zar level**: the divisor-functor map intertwines
331	the Picard classes with the Čech-Picard pullback, `𝒪(f*D) = f*𝒪(D)`.  Identical to the
332	chart-typed `DivFamZar.picClass_mapAlg` — the class never saw the cover. -/
333	lemma DivFamZarAff.picClass_mapAlg (F : DivFamZarAff C R n) :
334	    (DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R' n F).picClass =
335	      Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C R R') F.picClass := by
336	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
337	  | h d => exact Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback (relCurveMap C R R') d.1 _
338	
339	/-- **The identity functor law** at the widened Zar level. -/
340	lemma DivFamZarAff.mapAlg_id (F : DivFamZarAff C R n) :
341	    DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R n F = F := by
342	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
343	  | h d =>
344	      exact DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr
345	        (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback_id relCurveMap_id d.1 _)
346	
347	end Transport

357	    DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R'' n (DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R' n F)
358	      = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R'' n F := by
359	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with

363	          (relCurveMap_comp (R' := R') (R'' := R'')) d.1 _ _ _)

367	/-! ## Zariski separation at the widened Zar level -/
368	
369	/-- **Zariski separation of the widened divisor functor**: two widened classes agreeing under
370	`mapAlg` on every member of a finite covering family of localizations agree.
371	
372	Certificates play no role in equality, so — exactly as for `DivFamZar.eq_of_away_eq` — this
373	reduces verbatim to the `DivEq`-level engine `divEq_of_divEq_pullback`, and the widening is
374	invisible.  Note this needs `[IsProper C.hom]` only because `mapAlg` does. -/
375	theorem DivFamZarAff.eq_of_away_eq [IsProper C.hom] {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (g : ι → R)
376	    (S : ι → Type u)
377	    [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra R (S i)]
378	    [∀ i, IsScalarTower k R (S i)] [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]
379	    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤) {F G : DivFamZarAff C R n}
380	    (h : ∀ i, DivFamZarAff.mapAlg (S i) n F = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg (S i) n G) :
381	    F = G := by
382	  haveI : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (S i)) := fun i =>
383	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (S i) (g i)
384	  revert h
385	  refine Quotient.inductionOn₂ F G fun d₁ d₂ h => ?_
386	  refine DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr ?_
387	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_of_divEq_pullback
388	    (fun i => relCurveMap C R (S i))
389	    (fun y => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R g S hg y)
390	    (fun i => d₁.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (S i) n)
391	    (fun i => d₂.2.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors (S i) n)
392	    (fun i => ?_)
393	  exact DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mp (h i)

395	/-! ## Obligation I-0492 4(i) read on the FIBRE CURVE
396	
397	The widened assembler's fibrewise-regularity input (`hfib` of
398	`AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy`, `DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean`) is stated as a
399	tensor condition: `eqn j ⊗ 1` is a nonzerodivisor in `Γ(pieces j) ⊗[R] κ(p)`.  Protection
400	I-0492 clause 4(i) says that datum must come from the seed's own degree data, and a tensor
401	product is not the shape any geometric argument produces.
402	
403	The section base change of this file's upstream turns it into the shape that IS produced:
404	`Γ(pieces j) ⊗[R] κ(p) ≅ Γ(relCurve C κ(p), relCurveMap ⁻¹ᵁ pieces j)`, so `hfib` at `p` says
405	exactly that the **pulled equation is regular on the fibre curve over `κ(p)`** — a statement
406	about a section of a sheaf on a curve over a field, checkable germ by germ.
407	
408	This is a restatement, not a discharge: the obligation stays an obligation, as clause 4(i)
409	requires.  What changes is that it is now stated in the vocabulary the seed layer speaks.  -/
410	
411	section Fibre
412	
413	variable {n}
414	
415	/-- **The fibrewise-regularity obligation, read on the fibre curve.**  `eqn j ⊗ 1` is a
416	nonzerodivisor in `Γ(pieces j) ⊗[R] κ(p)` **iff** the compared equation is a nonzerodivisor in
417	the sections of the fibre curve over `κ(p)` on the preimage of the piece.
418	
419	Both directions are the same ring isomorphism, so this is an honest translation with no
420	hypothesis beyond affineness of the piece — which is a field of `AffCoverData`. -/
421	theorem AffAdaptation.eqn_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff {D : AffCoverData C R}
422	    {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations} (A : AffAdaptation D d) (j : D.index)
423	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
424	    (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
425	        Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
426	      nonZeroDivisors (Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)
427	    ↔ relAffSectionsMap C p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.pieces j) (A.eqn j) ∈
428	        nonZeroDivisors
429	          Γ(relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
430	            relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces j) := by
431	  let e : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField ≃+*
432	      Γ(relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
433	        relCurveMap C R p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces j) :=
434	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
435	        p.asIdeal.ResidueField).toRingEquiv.trans
436	      (relSectionsBaseChangeAff C p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.isAffineOpen j)).toRingEquiv
437	  have hval : e (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
438	      = relAffSectionsMap C p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.pieces j) (A.eqn j) := by
439	    change (relSectionsBaseChangeAff C p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.isAffineOpen j))
440	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)
441	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField))) = _
442	    rw [Algebra.TensorProduct.comm_tmul,
443	      relSectionsBaseChangeAff_one_tmul C p.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.isAffineOpen j)]
444	  refine ⟨fun h => hval ▸ map_mem_nonZeroDivisors' e h, fun h => ?_⟩
445	  have hback := map_mem_nonZeroDivisors' e.symm (hval ▸ h)
446	  rwa [e.symm_apply_apply] at hback
447	
448	end Fibre
