450	/-! ## `toAff` is a map of FUNCTORS, not just of values
451	
452	`DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean` gave `DivFamZar.toAff` on values.  With `mapAlg` in place the
453	comparison can be checked to be natural, which is what a consumer needs in order to move
454	between the two values at will: both sides pull back the SAME representative system, and the
455	two `mk`s are equal because the setoids are the same `DivEq` relation. -/
456	
457	/-- **`toAff` commutes with base change.**  So a consumer may transport a chart-typed class and
458	then widen, or widen and then transport, and get the same widened class. -/
459	lemma DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlg [IsProper C.hom] {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
460	    (F : DivFamZar C R π n) :
461	    (DivFamZar.mapAlg R' n F).toAff = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R' n F.toAff := by
462	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
463	  | h d => exact DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _)
464

11	/-!
12	# The consumed local divisor package for the rank-one route
13	
14	This module is the first divisor consumer of PicRankOneLocalPresentation.  The projective
15	rank-one H0 module supplies a basic open and a section which is nonzero on every residue fibre
16	there.  The datum-side section construction then gives regular local equations, and the widened
17	effectivity engine packages those equations as a DivFamZarAff of degree genus C.

19	The package is deliberately local and presentation-tied.  It does not define the canonical
20	family-level divisorOfRankOne, identify the equations with the native zero locus, or assert
21	that the rank-one locus is represented by an open subscheme.  Those remain the next contracts.

8	/-!
9	# Pullback of local-equation divisors and its Picard class
10	
11	For a morphism of schemes `f : Y ⟶ X` and a local-equation system `E : X.LocalEquations`
12	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorClass`), this file constructs the pulled-back system
13	`E.pullback f hreg : Y.LocalEquations`, whose equations are the `f`-pullbacks of the
14	equations of `E`, living on the pulled-back pointed cover `E.cover.pullback f`
15	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.UnitsCocycle`). Its Picard class is the pullback of the class
16	of `E`:
17	
18	`(E.pullback f hreg).picClass = CechPic.map f E.picClass`.
19	
20	## The regularity side-hypothesis
21	
22	The naive statement — "pull the equations back and stay a `LocalEquations`" — is **false**
23	without a side-condition: a nonzerodivisor can pull back to a zerodivisor along a non-flat
24	morphism, so the `regular` field of the target need not hold. The construction therefore
25	takes the regularity of the *pulled-back* equations as an explicit hypothesis `hreg`: for
26	every point `z` of the member `(E.cover.pullback f).opens y`, the germ of the pulled-back
27	equation `pullbackEqn f E y` at `z` is a nonzerodivisor. This is the primitive form of the
28	side-condition (option (a) of the deg-D4 recon): it is exactly what a downstream user
29	(e.g. presenting a graph as the pullback of a diagonal) proves from the *relative-divisor*
30	geometry that makes the pulled equations regular, and it is discharged pointwise. A
31	flatness assumption on `f` is a stronger sufficient condition; it would be a corollary of
32	this primitive, not the primitive itself.
33	
34	## Main declarations
35	
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn`: the `f`-pullback of the equation
37	  `E.eqn (f.base y)` to the member `(E.cover.pullback f).opens y`, via `Scheme.Hom.appLE`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback`: the pulled-back local-equation system
39	  on `E.cover.pullback f`, under the regularity hypothesis `hreg`.
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullback_ratioUnit`: the transition units of the
41	  pulled-back system are the `f`-pullbacks (`Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`) of the transition units
42	  of `E`.
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback`: the Picard class of the
44	  pulled-back system is `CechPic.map f` applied to the class of `E`.
45	-/

61	/-! ## The pulled-back equations -/
62	
63	/-- The `f`-pullback of the local equation `E.eqn (f.base y)` to the member
64	`(E.cover.pullback f).opens y = f ⁻¹ᵁ E.cover.opens (f.base y)` of the pulled-back pointed
65	cover. This is the section that the pulled-back system carries on that member. -/
66	noncomputable def pullbackEqn (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (y : Y) :
67	    Γ(Y, (E.cover.pullback f).opens y) :=
68	  (f.appLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y)) ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y) le_rfl).hom
69	    (E.eqn (f.base y))
70	
71	/-- Restriction of a pulled-back equation to a sub-open `W ≤ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y`
72	is the `f`-pullback of `E.eqn (f.base y)` directly to `W`. This is the ring-level naturality
73	of `appLE` with restriction (`Scheme.Hom.appLE_map`), packaged for the ratio computation. -/
74	lemma pullbackEqn_res (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (y : Y) {W : Y.Opens}
75	    (h : W ≤ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y) :
76	    (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom (pullbackEqn f E y)
77	      = (f.appLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y)) W (h.trans le_rfl)).hom (E.eqn (f.base y)) := by
78	  rw [pullbackEqn, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.appLE_map]
79	
80	/-! ## The ratio equation -/
81	
82	/-- The defining ratio equation of the pulled-back system on the overlap
83	`(E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y'`: the two pulled-back
84	equations differ by the `f`-pullback (`Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`) of the transition unit
85	`E.ratioUnit (f.base y) (f.base y')`. -/
86	lemma pullback_ratio_eq (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (y y' : Y) :
87	    (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
88	        (E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y'
89	          ≤ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y)).op).hom (pullbackEqn f E y)
90	      = ((f.unitsAppLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y) ⊓ E.cover.opens (f.base y'))
91	            ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y')
92	            (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
93	            (E.ratioUnit (f.base y) (f.base y')))
94	          : Γ(Y, (E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y'))
95	        * (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
96	            (E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y'
97	              ≤ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y')).op).hom (pullbackEqn f E y') := by
98	  have key := congrArg
99	    (f.appLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y) ⊓ E.cover.opens (f.base y'))
100	      ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y')
101	      (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)).hom
102	    (E.eqn_restrict_eq (f.base y) (f.base y'))
103	  rw [map_mul, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.map_appLE,
104	    ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, Scheme.Hom.map_appLE] at key
105	  rw [pullbackEqn_res, pullbackEqn_res, Scheme.Hom.coe_unitsAppLE]
106	  exact key
107	
108	/-! ## The pulled-back local-equation system -/
109	
110	/-- The pullback of a local-equation system `E` along a morphism `f : Y ⟶ X`, under the
111	side-hypothesis `hreg` that the pulled-back equations are regular (their germs are
112	nonzerodivisors at every point of their member).
113	
114	The equations are the `f`-pullbacks `pullbackEqn f E y` of the equations of `E`, living on
115	the pulled-back pointed cover `E.cover.pullback f`. Regularity is supplied by `hreg` — it is
116	not automatic, since pulling a nonzerodivisor back along a non-flat morphism may produce a
117	zerodivisor. The overlap ratios are the `f`-pullbacks of the ratios of `E`, hence units. -/
118	noncomputable def pullback (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations)
119	    (hreg : ∀ (y z : Y) (hz : z ∈ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y),
120	      (Y.presheaf.germ ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y) z hz).hom (pullbackEqn f E y)
121	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors (Y.presheaf.stalk z)) :
122	    Y.LocalEquations where
123	  cover := E.cover.pullback f
124	  eqn y := pullbackEqn f E y
125	  regular := hreg
126	  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
127	    ⟨f.unitsAppLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y) ⊓ E.cover.opens (f.base y'))
128	        ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y')
129	        (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
130	        (E.ratioUnit (f.base y) (f.base y')),
131	      pullback_ratio_eq f E y y'⟩
132	
133	@[simp]
134	lemma pullback_cover (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) :
135	    (E.pullback f hreg).cover = E.cover.pullback f :=
136	  rfl
137	
138	@[simp]
139	lemma pullback_eqn (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) (y : Y) :
140	    (E.pullback f hreg).eqn y = pullbackEqn f E y :=
141	  rfl
142	
143	/-- The transition units of the pulled-back system are the `f`-pullbacks
144	(`Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`) of the transition units of `E`. -/
145	lemma pullback_ratioUnit (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) (y y' : Y) :
146	    (E.pullback f hreg).ratioUnit y y'
147	      = f.unitsAppLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y) ⊓ E.cover.opens (f.base y'))
148	          ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y')
149	          (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
150	          (E.ratioUnit (f.base y) (f.base y')) :=
151	  ((E.pullback f hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y' _ (pullback_ratio_eq f E y y')).symm
152	
153	/-! ## The Picard class of a pullback -/
154	
155	/-- The cocycle of transition units of the pulled-back system is the `f`-pullback of the
156	cocycle of `E` (`Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle`). -/
157	lemma pullback_unitsCocycle (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) :
158	    (E.pullback f hreg).unitsCocycle = f.pullbackUnitsCocycle E.unitsCocycle := by
159	  refine unitsCocycle_ext fun y y' ↦ ?_
160	  calc unitsEvInf (E.pullback f hreg).unitsCocycle y y'
161	      = f.unitsAppLE (E.cover.opens (f.base y) ⊓ E.cover.opens (f.base y'))
162	          ((E.cover.pullback f).opens y ⊓ (E.cover.pullback f).opens y')
163	          (f.le_preimage_inf inf_le_left inf_le_right)
164	          (E.ratioUnit (f.base y) (f.base y')) :=
165	        ((E.pullback f hreg).unitsCocycle_evInf y y').trans (pullback_ratioUnit f E hreg y y')
166	    _ = unitsEvInf (f.pullbackUnitsCocycle E.unitsCocycle) y y' := by
167	        rw [Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsCocycle_unitsEvInf, unitsCocycle_evInf]
168	
169	/-- The Picard class of a pulled-back local-equation system is `CechPic.map f` applied to
170	the class of `E`: pulling back the divisor pulls back its class `𝒪(D)`. -/
171	@[simp]
172	lemma picClass_pullback (f : Y ⟶ X) (E : X.LocalEquations) (hreg) :
173	    (E.pullback f hreg).picClass = CechPic.map f E.picClass := by
174	  change CechPic.mk (E.cover.pullback f) (E.pullback f hreg).unitsCocycle.class
175	    = CechPic.map f (CechPic.mk E.cover E.unitsCocycle.class)
176	  rw [CechPic.map_mk, Scheme.Hom.pullbackUnitsH1_class]
177	  exact congrArg (CechPic.mk (E.cover.pullback f))
178	    (congrArg OneCocycle.class (pullback_unitsCocycle f E hreg))
179

56	/-! ## Divisor equality of local-equation systems (the setoid relation)
57	
58	Generic in the scheme; this is pure `DivisorClass`-level material. -/

63	
64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
69	
70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
79	
80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
82	
83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
89	
90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
115	        exact E1
116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
122	        rw [E2]
123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
125	        rw [mul_assoc]
126	
127	/-- Structure extensionality for local-equation systems: the two `Prop` fields are
128	proof-irrelevant, so a system is determined by its cover and equations. -/
129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)
130	    (heqn : d.eqn ≍ e.eqn) : d = e := by
131	  cases d; cases e
132	  cases hcov; cases heqn
133	  rfl
134	
135	/-- **Divisor equality preserves the Picard class** (`𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor):
136	restrict both systems to the common refinement (`picClass_restrict`), where they differ
137	by a unit rescaling (`picClass_rescale`). -/
138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
139	    d₁.picClass = d₂.picClass := by
140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
141	  rw [← d₁.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₁, ← d₂.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₂]
142	  have hres : d₁.restrict 𝒲 h₁ = (d₂.restrict 𝒲 h₂).rescale (fun x => (H x).choose) := by
143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
144	    exact (H x).choose_spec
145	  rw [hres, picClass_rescale]
146	
147	end Scheme.LocalEquations

60	/-- `appLE` of a local equation at propositionally equal base points. -/
61	private lemma appLE_eqn_congr {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) (E : Y.LocalEquations)
62	    {x₁ x₂ : Y} (hx : x₁ = x₂) {W : X.Opens}
63	    (e₁ : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ E.cover.opens x₁) (e₂ : W ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ E.cover.opens x₂) :

69	/-- **Divisor equality is stable under pullback**: a common refinement with pointwise
70	units pulls back to a common refinement with pulled units (`Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE`). -/
71	theorem divEq_pullback {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : Y ⟶ X) {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations}
72	    (h : DivEq d₁ d₂)
73	    (hreg₁ : ∀ (y z : Y) (hz : z ∈ (d₁.cover.pullback f).opens y),
74	      (Y.presheaf.germ ((d₁.cover.pullback f).opens y) z hz).hom (pullbackEqn f d₁ y)

/-! ## Pointed covers -/

/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. Pointed covers
are the index discipline of `Scheme.CechPic`: the index type is the carrier of `X` (so
everything stays in `Type u`), refinement is indexwise, and pointwise `⊓` makes the
refinement order directed. -/
structure PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
  /-- The member of the cover attached to a point. -/
  opens : X → X.Opens
  /-- Each point lies in its member. -/
  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x

namespace PointedCover

@[ext]
lemma ext {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : ∀ x, 𝒰.opens x = 𝒱.opens x) : 𝒰 = 𝒱 := by
  cases 𝒰; cases 𝒱
  simpa using funext h

instance : SemilatticeInf X.PointedCover where
  le 𝒱 𝒰 := ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x
  le_refl 𝒰 x := le_rfl
  le_trans 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := (h₁ x).trans (h₂ x)
  le_antisymm 𝒰 𝒱 h₁ h₂ := ext fun x ↦ le_antisymm (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
  inf 𝒰 𝒱 :=
    { opens := fun x ↦ 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x
      mem_opens := fun x ↦ ⟨𝒰.mem_opens x, 𝒱.mem_opens x⟩ }
  inf_le_left 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_left
  inf_le_right 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_right
  le_inf 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := le_inf (h₁ x) (h₂ x)

instance : OrderTop X.PointedCover where
  top := { opens := fun _ ↦ ⊤, mem_opens := fun _ ↦ trivial }
  le_top _ _ := le_top

lemma le_def {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x :=
  Iff.rfl

@[simp]
lemma inf_opens (𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (x : X) :
    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x = 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x :=
  rfl

@[simp]
lemma top_opens (x : X) : (⊤ : X.PointedCover).opens x = ⊤ :=
  rfl

/-- The pullback of a pointed cover along a morphism of schemes: the pointed cover by
preimages, `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`. -/
def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) : X.PointedCover where
  opens x := f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x)
  mem_opens x := 𝒰.mem_opens (f.base x)

@[simp]
lemma pullback_opens (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (x : X) :
    (𝒰.pullback f).opens x = f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x) :=
  rfl

lemma pullback_mono (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 𝒱 : Y.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) :
    𝒱.pullback f ≤ 𝒰.pullback f :=
  fun x ↦ ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f.base).map (homOfLE (h (f.base x)))).le

end PointedCover

/-- **`appLE` commutes with restriction**: for `f : X ⟶ Y`, restricting the `appLE`
image of a section equals the `appLE` image of the restricted section. Both sides are

  have h1 := congr((CommRingCat.Hom.hom

666	The rank-one field of `P` makes every residue-field fibre of its `H⁰` module nontrivial.
667	The projective-module generator lemma therefore supplies a single basic open `D(f)` and
668	one datum section `y` which stays nonzero on every residue fibre over that open.  The same
669	`y` is transported to a native global section and its unit-lift through the evaluation

30	  N5 engine input): a second element `q'` lies in the `B_f`-span of the local basis `q`,
31	  so `q' = a • q` in `Q_f` for a scalar `a`.

34	consume the local basis to rescale the two canonical sections by a unit

49	/-- **The Nakayama companion — a fibrewise-nonzero element is a Zariski-local basis**
50	(worksheet GAP-3 companion, deferred from C2/I-0253): for a finite projective `B`-module
51	`Q` of stalk-rank exactly `1` at the prime `p`, an element `q : Q` whose image in the
52	fibre `Q ⊗ κ(p)` is nonzero generates `Q` freely on a basic open `D(f) ∋ p`: the map
53	`x ↦ x • q` is a bijection `B_f → Q_f`.
54	
55	Over the local ring `Rₚ` the localized module `Qₚ` is free of rank `1`, so `q`'s basis
56	coordinate `c` satisfies: if `c` were a non-unit it would lie in the maximal ideal, hence
57	`q` would vanish in the fibre `κ(p) ⊗ Qₚ ≅ Q ⊗ κ(p)`, contradicting `hq`. Thus `c` is a
58	unit and `q` spans `Qₚ`; `Module.Invertible`'s `bijective_of_surjective` promotes spanning
59	to a bijection, and the isomorphism spreads to a basic open. -/
60	theorem exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton
61	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q] (p : PrimeSpectrum B)
62	    (hrank : Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1) (q : Q)
63	    (hq : (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
64	    ∃ f : B, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ Function.Bijective
65	      (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers f) (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) := by
66	  classical
67	  haveI : Module.FinitePresentation B Q := Module.finitePresentation_of_projective B Q
68	  set Rₚ := Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal with hRₚ
69	  set Qₚ := LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q with hQₚ
70	  set mkq : Qₚ := LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q q with hmkq
71	  -- `Qₚ` is finite, flat and hence free of rank `1` over the local ring `Rₚ`
72	  haveI : Module.Free Rₚ Qₚ := Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing
73	  have hrank1 : Module.finrank Rₚ Qₚ = 1 := hrank
74	  -- a basis of the free rank-`1` module, and the coordinate of `mkq`
75	  set b : Module.Basis Unit Rₚ Qₚ := Module.basisUnique Unit hrank1 with hb
76	  set c : Rₚ := b.repr mkq default with hc
77	  have hmkq_eq : mkq = c • b default := by
78	    have hsum := b.sum_repr mkq
79	    rw [Fintype.sum_unique, ← hc] at hsum
80	    exact hsum.symm
81	  -- `c` is a unit: otherwise `mkq` vanishes in the fibre, contradicting `hq`
82	  have hcunit : IsUnit c := by
83	    rw [← IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal]
84	    intro hcmem
85	    -- the fibre map `κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ → κ ⊗[B] Q` sends `1 ⊗ mkq` to `1 ⊗ q`, injectively
86	    set κ := p.asIdeal.ResidueField with hκ
87	    set η : Qₚ ≃ₗ[Rₚ] Rₚ ⊗[B] Q := LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q
88	      with hη
89	    set ε : κ ⊗[Rₚ] Qₚ →ₗ[Rₚ] κ ⊗[B] Q :=
90	      (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange B Rₚ κ κ Q).toLinearMap.restrictScalars Rₚ
91	        ∘ₗ (η.lTensor κ).toLinearMap with hε
92	    have hηmkq : η mkq = (1 : Rₚ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
93	      rw [hη, hmkq, LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap_apply,
94	        LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct_apply_mk, Localization.mk_one]
95	    have hεval : ε ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq) = (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q := by
96	      simp only [hε, LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe,
97	        LinearEquiv.lTensor_tmul, hηmkq,
98	        TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]
99	    -- but `1 ⊗ mkq = 0` since `c ∈ maximalIdeal` kills the residue
100	    have hcres : c • (1 : κ) = 0 := by
101	      rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_one, IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq]
102	      exact (IsLocalRing.residue_eq_zero_iff c).mpr hcmem
103	    have hzero : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[Rₚ] mkq = 0 := by
104	      rw [hmkq_eq, ← TensorProduct.smul_tmul, hcres, TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
105	    -- transport the vanishing to `Q ⊗ κ`, contradicting `hq`
106	    have h1q : (1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q = 0 := by rw [← hεval, hzero, map_zero]
107	    exact hq (by
108	      rw [show (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : κ) : Q ⊗[B] κ)
109	          = TensorProduct.comm B κ Q ((1 : κ) ⊗ₜ[B] q) from rfl, h1q, map_zero])
110	  -- `mkq` spans `Qₚ` (unit multiple of a basis element), so `toSpanSingleton` is surjective
111	  haveI hinv : Module.Invertible Rₚ Qₚ :=
112	    Module.Invertible.congr ((Module.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq_one hrank1).some)
113	  have hspanmkq : Submodule.span Rₚ {mkq} = ⊤ := by
114	    refine top_le_iff.mp ?_
115	    rw [← b.span_eq, Set.range_unique, Submodule.span_le, Set.singleton_subset_iff,
116	      SetLike.mem_coe]
117	    refine Submodule.mem_span_singleton.mpr ⟨(hcunit.unit⁻¹ : Rₚˣ).val, ?_⟩
118	    rw [hmkq_eq, smul_smul, hcunit.val_inv_mul, one_smul]
119	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Rₚ Qₚ mkq) := by
120	    rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, LinearMap.range_toSpanSingleton]; exact hspanmkq
121	  have hbijR : Function.Bijective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Rₚ Qₚ mkq) :=
122	    Module.Invertible.bijective_of_surjective hsurj
123	  -- identify the stalk of `toSpanSingleton` with `toSpanSingleton` over `Rₚ`
124	  have hmapeq : IsLocalizedModule.map p.asIdeal.primeCompl (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ)
125	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q) (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)
126	      = (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton Rₚ Qₚ mkq).restrictScalars B := by
127	    refine IsLocalizedModule.ext p.asIdeal.primeCompl (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ)
128	      (IsLocalizedModule.map_units (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)) ?_
129	    refine LinearMap.ext fun x => ?_
130	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.comp_apply, IsLocalizedModule.map_apply]
131	    simp only [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, LinearMap.restrictScalars_apply,
132	      Algebra.linearMap_apply, map_smul, ← hmkq]
133	    exact algebra_compatible_smul Rₚ x mkq
134	  have hstalk : Function.Bijective (IsLocalizedModule.map p.asIdeal.primeCompl
135	      (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ) (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q)
136	      (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) := by
137	    rw [hmapeq]; exact hbijR
138	  exact Module.FinitePresentation.exists_notMem_bijective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)
139	    p.asIdeal (Algebra.linearMap B Rₚ)
140	    (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.asIdeal.primeCompl Q) hstalk

142	/-- A fibrewise-nonzero element of a finite projective module of constant stalk rank one
143	is a global basis.  The local basis neighbourhoods supplied by
144	`exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton` cover `Spec B`: if their generators failed to
145	span the unit ideal, a maximal ideal containing that span would contain the generator
146	chosen at its own prime.  Bijectivity then descends from this standard-open cover. -/
147	theorem bijective_toSpanSingleton_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero
148	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q]
149	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1)
150	    (q : Q)
151	    (hq : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
152	      (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
153	        Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
154	    Function.Bijective (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q) := by
155	  classical
156	  let f : PrimeSpectrum B → B := fun p ↦
157	    (exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton p (hrank p) q (hq p)).choose
158	  have hf (p : PrimeSpectrum B) : f p ∉ p.asIdeal :=
159	    (exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton p (hrank p) q (hq p)).choose_spec.1
160	  have hbij (p : PrimeSpectrum B) : Function.Bijective
161	      (LocalizedModule.map (Submonoid.powers (f p))
162	        (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)) :=
163	    (exists_notMem_bijective_toSpanSingleton p (hrank p) q (hq p)).choose_spec.2
164	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ := by
165	    by_contra hne
166	    obtain ⟨m, hm, hle⟩ := Ideal.exists_le_maximal _ hne
167	    let p : PrimeSpectrum B := ⟨m, hm.isPrime⟩
168	    exact hf p (hle (Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self p)))
169	  refine bijective_of_localized_span (Set.range f) hspan
170	    (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q) ?_
171	  rintro ⟨r, p, rfl⟩
172	  exact hbij p

174	/-- Two fibrewise-nonzero elements of a finite projective module of constant stalk rank
175	one differ by a unique unit.  This is the choice-independence form consumed by the
176	rank-one divisor construction. -/
177	theorem existsUnique_unit_smul_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero
178	    [Module.Finite B Q] [Module.Projective B Q]
179	    (hrank : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, Module.rankAtStalk Q p = 1)
180	    (q q' : Q)
181	    (hq : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
182	      (q ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
183	        Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
184	    (hq' : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B,
185	      (q' ⊗ₜ[B] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
186	        Q ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
187	    ∃! u : Bˣ, q' = (u : B) • q := by
188	  let e : B ≃ₗ[B] Q := LinearEquiv.ofBijective
189	    (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton B Q q)
190	    (bijective_toSpanSingleton_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero hrank q hq)
191	  let a : B := e.symm q'
192	  have ha : q' = a • q := by
193	    rw [← LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply]
194	    exact (e.apply_symm_apply q').symm
195	  have hqbij := bijective_toSpanSingleton_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero hrank q hq
196	  have hq'bij := bijective_toSpanSingleton_of_forall_tmul_ne_zero hrank q' hq'
197	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hq'bij.2 q
198	  have hab : a * b = 1 := by
199	    apply hqbij.1
200	    rw [LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, LinearMap.toSpanSingleton_apply, one_smul]

/-!
# Base-change instances for the curve over an extension field (gap G-D5(a))

For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` (smooth of relative dimension one, proper and
geometrically irreducible over the field `k`) and a field extension `K` of `k`
(`[Field K] [Algebra k K]`), this file installs — **as instances that fire by typeclass
resolution** — every hypothesis of the landed degree/Riemann–Roch stack
(`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Degree`) for the base-changed curve

`C_K := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`,

viewed as a `K`-scheme via the **second projection** `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This is
exactly the `Over`-instance spelling that `Cohomology.RelativeTwoCover.relCurve.instOver`
uses (`.ofHom (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`), but keyed on the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`
spelling that the Riemann–Roch files consume, rather than on the `relCurve C K` `def`.

The single geometric input is the pullback bridge `AlgebraicGeometry.Over.isPullback_left`
(`Cohomology.SectionsBaseChange`): the second projection `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left` is the
base change of the structure morphism `C.hom` along `overSpec k K ⟶ Spec k`. Every morphism
property then transports by `MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange` (smooth of relative
dimension one, proper, geometrically irreducible), and integrality of `C_K` is
`isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced` applied to the base change (geometric
irreducibility is transported; geometric reducedness comes for free from smoothness).

## Main instances (keyed for the Riemann–Roch stack)

* `AlgebraicGeometry.instOverBaseChange` — item 1: `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` is a `K`-scheme
  via the second projection; `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec K = (snd C (overSpec k K)).left`
  definitionally (`baseChange_over_eq_snd_left`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft`,
  `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperSndLeft`,
  `AlgebraicGeometry.instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft` — the base-change transport of the
  standing bundle onto the raw morphism `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` (item 2),
  `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperBaseChange`,
  `AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactBaseChange` (item 4) — the same properties in the

* `AlgebraicGeometry.instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange`,

The acceptance smoke test (item 6) verifies that the landed `classDeg K` typechecks on `C_K`

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
  (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]

/-! ## Item 1: the `K`-scheme structure via the second projection -/

/-- **Item 1.** The base-changed curve `C_K := (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` is a scheme over
`Spec K` via the **second projection** `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This is the same
structure morphism that `Cohomology.RelativeTwoCover.relCurve.instOver` installs, but keyed on
the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` spelling consumed by the Riemann–Roch/degree stack (rather than
on the `relCurve C K` `def`). -/
noncomputable instance instOverBaseChange :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left).Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
  .ofHom (snd C (overSpec k K)).left

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
/-- The structure morphism installed by `instOverBaseChange` is, definitionally, the second
projection `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`. This equation is `rfl`; it lets a consumer rewrite
the `↘`-spelling that `classDeg` uses into the raw projection the base-change lemmas produce
(and back), and pins the alignment with `relCurve.instOver`. -/
theorem baseChange_over_eq_snd_left :
    ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) = (snd C (overSpec k K)).left :=
  rfl

/-! ## Transport of the standing bundle onto the raw second projection

Every property is transported from `C.hom` along the base-change square
`Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k K)`, whose right leg is the second projection. These are
keyed on the raw morphism `(snd C (overSpec k K)).left`, which is what the bundled curve
`Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k K)).left` feeds to the landed curve-level instances
(`isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced`, `moduleFinite_hModule_zero`/`_one`). -/

/-- **Base change of smooth-of-relative-dimension-one.** The second projection is smooth of
relative dimension one over `K`, by `smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange`. -/
instance instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft :
    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (snd C (overSpec k K)).left :=
  haveI : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1

noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
  comp f g := f ≫ g
  id_comp := Category.id_comp
  comp_id := Category.comp_id
  assoc := Category.assoc

-- data
/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)

-- data
/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
